item.title: Isaiah Jackson (LAC): Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings.
item.description:
Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings.

Dunn is good to go after missing most of the preseason with a minor injury, and he’ll start alongside Garland in the backcourt. Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said on Saturday that Jackson would start at center, so his inclusion is unsurprising. Garland and Hachimura should lead the starters offensively.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Tomer Azarly

item.title: [Injury] Malik Monk (SAC): Malik Monk (ankle) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Clippers.
item.description:
Malik Monk (ankle) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Clippers.

Initially questionable for Wednesday’s season opener, Monk’s status is trending in the wrong direction. If he can’t play, rookie Emanuel Sharp’s role could expand, but he won’t be worth the streaming risk in most leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Injury Report

item.title: [Injury] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said on Wednesday that he’s hopeful Brandin Podziemski (back) will return for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said on Wednesday that he’s hopeful Brandin Podziemski (back) will return for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.

After missing practice on Monday, Podziemski will miss Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers due to lower back soreness. However, he may not be out long, with Kerr hoping Podz can play on Friday. De’Anthony Melton is the player whose role may expand the most while Podziemski sits.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Anthony Slater

item.title: [Injury] Luke Kennard (PHX): Luke Kennard (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Luke Kennard (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.

Kennard will miss the Suns’ season opener after initially being listed as questionable. His absence likely means fellow reserve Jordan Goodwin will get more minutes.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Duane Rankin

item.title: [Injury] Adou Thiero (LAL): Adou Thiero (knee) has been shut down for a few days after experiencing swelling.
item.description:
Adou Thiero (knee) has been shut down for a few days after experiencing swelling.

Thiero will not play in Wednesday’s opener against the Warriors due to a right knee effusion. There has also been some swelling in the knee, so the Lakers are shutting the second-year wing down for a few days. Upon his clearance to resume working out, Thiero will be considered day-to-day.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Khobi Price

item.title: [Injury] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija (ankle) is a game time decision against the Suns in Wednesday’s season opener.
item.description:
Deni Avdija (ankle) is a game time decision against the Suns in Wednesday’s season opener.

The Blazers already have Shaedon Sharpe out for an extended of of time. If Deni were to miss time, there would be more minutes for Sidy Cissoko and Vit Krecji, but neither would be that impactful in most fantasy leagues.

Fonte: Duane Rankin

item.title: [Injury] Cameron Carr (LAL): According to Lakers head coach JJ Redick, Cameron Carr (oblique) is “ramping up” and is day-to-day moving forward.
item.description:
According to Lakers head coach JJ Redick, Cameron Carr (oblique) is “ramping up” and is day-to-day moving forward.

Carr, who played well during Summer League, was ruled out for Wednesday’s opener with a strained oblique. The good news is that a return to action may not be far away, with the rookie now considered day-to-day, according to Redick. Carr should slide into the back end of the Lakers’ perimeter rotation once cleared to play.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Jovan Buha

item.title: Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, Cooper Flagg, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Wednesday’s game against the Rockets.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, Cooper Flagg, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Wednesday’s game against the Rockets.

Christie and Flagg were the only starters to take on that role in the Mavericks’ final game of the 2025-26 season. Irving, Washington, and Gafford are back from injury and will round out the starting five on Opening Night. It’s unclear whether Irving’s minutes will be limited, but don’t be surprised if the Mavericks don’t ask him to take on a full workload immediately.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Lineups

item.title: Kevin Durant (HOU): Rockets start Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun against the Mavericks on Wednesday.
item.description:
Rockets start Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun against the Mavericks on Wednesday.

Durant is 38 and entering his 19th season in the NBA, but he showed few signs of slowing down last season as he was named to the league’s All-NBA second-team. He’ll start alongside VanVleet, Thompson, Smith and Sengun against the Mavericks on Wednesday.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Injury] Julian Phillips (HOU): Julian Phillips (illness) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks.
item.description:
Julian Phillips (illness) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks.

Phillips is good to go after initially being questionable for Wednesday’s season opener. However, with the Rockets largely healthy on the perimeter, the two-way contract wing is unlikely to get the minutes needed to affect fantasy basketball.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: NBA Injury Report

item.title: Bilal Coulibaly: The Wizards will start Trae Young, Kyshawn George, Bilal Coulibaly, Anthony Davis, and Alex Sarr against Bucks on Wednesday
item.description:
The Wizards will start Trae Young, Kyshawn George, Bilal Coulibaly, Anthony Davis, and Alex Sarr against Bucks on Wednesday
